decisions.reason: As a low-cost service that supports the installed machine base, the training programme is likely to stay unless demand clearly falls below aspirations, and an established medium-sized firm has some slack to carry it.

The fourth rotary axis accessory is closely related to the firm's core machinery offer, so even if sales are only moderate management would likely keep it as a complementary option rather than redeploy resources immediately.

Hybrid additive post-processing looks like the most exploratory and weakly embedded offer, so if its results have stayed below aspiration levels the firm would likely redirect resources back to core machining or more promising projects.

A high-speed CNC milling machine fits the firm's core business and likely had higher initial commitment, so management would tend to continue it unless performance was clearly and persistently disappointing.

The automatic tool change system complements the main machine business and can enhance customer value with limited extra slack consumption, making continued market presence more likely than withdrawal.
